title: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and Same-Region Replication (SRR)
hook: Amazon S3 replication asynchronously copies new objects to a destination bucket — same account or cross-account, same region or cross-region. It is ongoing disaster recovery and locality, not a one-time migration tool for existing objects.

blocks.text: Cross-Region Replication (CRR) copies objects to a bucket in another region. Same-Region Replication (SRR) copies within one region — often for log aggregation or compliance copies. Requires versioning on source and destination. Replication rule filters by prefix or tags. Replication Time Control (RTC) adds 15-minute SLA. Existing objects need S3 Batch Replication.

entries.plainDefinition: Automatic copy of new objects to another AWS region.
Replication within the same region to another bucket.
entries.example: App bucket → audit-log bucket same region.

entries.plainDefinition: Paid SLA for replication within 15 minutes.
entries.example: Regulated DR with S3 Replication Time metric.

entries.plainDefinition: One-time replication of existing objects before rule existed.
entries.example: Backfill 10 TB uploaded before CRR enabled.

blocks.text: Teams enable CRR and wonder why pre-existing data is missing in DR — replication is not retroactive. KMS key policies must allow replication role in both regions. Delete marker replication is optional — understand whether DR should see deletes.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: versioning required both buckets. New objects only unless Batch Replication. Check object replication status. RTC for minute-level RPO.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Enable versioning
items.body: Source and destination buckets both versioned.

items.title: Create replication rule
items.body: Destination bucket, IAM role, prefix filter optional.

items.title: KMS permissions
items.body: Replication role decrypt source CMK, encrypt destination CMK.

items.title: Backfill existing
items.body: S3 Batch Replication job for objects before rule.

diagram.title: CRR flow
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  PUT[PUT object\nus-east-1] --> SRC[(source bucket)]
  SRC -->|async replicate| DST[(dest bucket\neu-west-1)]
  SRC -->|status PENDING| META[object metadata]
  DST -->|status REPLICA| META

snippet.label: CLI — enable versioning and replication
snippet.explanation: RTC enabled in Destination.ReplicationTime. Prefix prod/ limits replication scope.

snippet.label: CLI — check object replication status
snippet.explanation: PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED, REPLICA — FAILED needs IAM or KMS fix.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — replication role trust policy excerpt
snippet.code:
Resources:
  ReplicationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: s3.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ReplicateObjects
          PolicyDocument:
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: [s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication, s3:ReplicateObject]
                Resource: ['arn:aws:s3:::primary-us-east-1/*', 'arn:aws:s3:::dr-eu-west-1/*']
snippet.explanation: S3 service assumes role for replication — not your application role.

snippet.label: CLI — S3 Batch Replication for backlog
snippet.explanation: Batch job replicates existing objects listed in manifest — run once after enabling CRR rule.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Expecting retroactive replication. Versioning off on destination. KMS key policy missing replication role. Bidirectional replication without delete marker strategy — delete loops.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: S3 Replication metrics OperationsPendingReplication, ReplicationLatency. Failover drill: promote DR bucket read, document RPO from RTC metric. Cross-account: destination bucket policy trusts source account replication role.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'enable CRR and all data copies.' Strong answer: versioning, new objects only, Batch for backlog, check FAILED status, KMS policies.

interviewTakeaways: CRR replicates new objects after rule — Batch Replication for existing backlog.
Versioning required on source and destination; check ReplicationStatus on objects.
RTC for 15-minute RPO SLA; standard CRR is best-effort async.
60s: Versioning both buckets. New objects only. Batch backlog. KMS role. FAILED status debug.
Follow-up: replicate delete markers yes or no for DR?
commonPitfalls: Missing pre-rule objects in DR — expected CRR behavior not bug.
Strong answer: run S3 Batch Replication manifest job once.
KMS FAILED replication status — key policy omission.

jsTsCorrelations.note: S3 CRR async copy parallels PostgreSQL async replica — lag exists, promote DR is failover not instant consistency.
